title: Behold a Stranger at the Door
description: Behold a Stranger at the Door in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Joseph Grigg wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 51.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold a Stran-ger at the door! He gen-tly knocks, has knocked be-fore, Has wait-ed long, is wait-ing still; You treat no oth-er friend so ill.

lines: Behold a Stranger at the door!
He gently knocks, has knocked before,
Has waited long, is waiting still;
You treat no other friend so ill.
But will He prove a friend indeed?
He will; the very Friend you need;
With melting heart and laden hands;
O matchless kindness! and He shows
This matchless kindness to His foes.
Admit Him lest His anger burn
Admit Him, or the hour’s at hand
When at His door denied you’ll stand.

licence: Public domain: Joseph Grigg died in 1768.
credits: Words by Joseph Grigg (1720–1768), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
